wing.title: Set up a new wing and its cells

sections.title: Create the wing and choose its structure
sections.intro: Have the wing code, its structure and the information about its cells ready before you start.

rows.title: Enter the wing details
rows.body: Enter a wing code and, if needed, a local name. The local name changes how the wing is displayed, without changing its code.
rows.alt: The Wing code and optional Local name fields are blank. The name counter shows 30 characters remaining.

rows.title: Choose the wing structure
rows.body: Set the levels to match the actual wing. This example uses spurs, landings and cells. Other wings may have a different structure.
rows.alt: The structure preview shows Wing at level 1, with Spurs, Landings and Cells nested below it at levels 2, 3 and 4.

rows.title: Check and create the wing
rows.body: Check its code, name and structure, then select Create wing. The new wing is a draft. Add its locations before requesting a change to the cell certificate.
rows.alt: The wing summary shows code ZZ and local name AAA, with a Change link next to each detail.

sections.title: Add spurs and landings
sections.intro: Follow the levels chosen for this wing. This example uses a spur and a landing.

rows.title: Add a spur
rows.body: From the draft wing, select Create new spur. Enter its code and optional local name.
rows.alt: The spur code field contains AAA after the wing prefix ZZ. The local name is A.

rows.title: Check and create the spur
rows.body: Check the spur details, then select Create spur. You can now add landings within it.
rows.alt: The spur summary shows code ZZ-AAA and local name A. The spur stays in draft until it is added to the cell certificate.

rows.title: Add a landing
rows.body: Select Create new landing. Enter its code and optional local name. Choose Yes to create its cells now, or create them later.
rows.alt: The landing code field contains AAA after the prefix ZZ-AAA. Yes is selected to create cells now.

sections.title: Create and number cells
sections.intro: Create the cells on the new landing and check their numbering.

rows.title: Enter the cell details
rows.body: Enter how many cells to create and select the accommodation type. This example creates eight cells on the new landing.
rows.alt: Normal accommodation is selected for 8 new cells on landing ZZ-AAA-AAA.

rows.title: Set the cell numbers
rows.body: Enter the starting number and select Apply to number the cells. Check each number before continuing.
rows.alt: The starting number is 1. The table shows cells ZZ-AAA-AAA-001 to ZZ-AAA-AAA-008.

rows.title: Enter the door numbers
rows.body: Enter the number written on each cell door. It may be different from the cell number used in Locations.
rows.alt: Door numbers 1 to 8 are entered alongside cell numbers ending in 001 to 008.

sections.title: Set capacities and other cell details
sections.intro: Check the capacities and other information for the cells you are creating.

rows.title: Set capacities and cell types
rows.body: Enter baseline CNA, working capacity and maximum capacity. Apply a value to all cells when appropriate, then check each row. Add a cell type where needed.
rows.alt: All 8 cells have a baseline CNA, working capacity and maximum capacity of 1. Each capacity field above the table has an Apply to all link.

rows.title: Record what the cells are used for
rows.body: Select the uses that apply to all the cells in this example. Check that the choices describe the accommodation you are creating.
rows.alt: Standard accommodation is the only use selected for the cells on the new landing.

rows.title: Record in-cell sanitation
rows.body: Confirm whether all the cells have both a toilet and a wash basin.
rows.alt: Yes is selected to confirm all cells on the new landing have a toilet and wash basin.

sections.title: Check locations and request approval
sections.intro: Creating draft locations and requesting approval are separate parts of the process.

rows.title: Check and create the locations
rows.body: Check the landing, cell numbers, capacities and other details. Use Change to correct anything, then select Create locations.
rows.alt: The summary shows landing ZZ-AAA-AAA and 8 cells. Each cell has capacities of 1 and sanitation marked Yes.

rows.title: Check the draft locations
rows.body: The landing and cells have been created in draft. Repeat the relevant steps for any other spurs, landings and cells you need.
rows.alt: The confirmation shows landing ZZ-AAA-AAA and 8 cells were created. The landing and all 8 cells are marked Draft.

rows.title: Add the wing to the cell certificate
rows.body: When the locations are ready, select Add wing to cell certificate. Adding new locations requires a change request.
rows.alt: The page explains that the authorising director must approve the change and shows a Continue button.

rows.title: Check and submit the request
rows.body: Review the proposed locations and capacities and the certification statement. When ready, select Submit for approval. The request goes to the establishment’s authorising director. Locations cannot be changed while it is reviewed.
rows.alt: The request lists the proposed wing, spur, landing and 8 cells. The certification statement has an unchecked agreement box above Submit for approval.

add-cells.title: Add cells to an existing location

sections.title: Find the location and create cells
sections.intro: Use this guide when the wing and landing already exist. Have the cell numbers, capacities and other cell information ready.

rows.title: Find the existing location
rows.body: Open Manage residential locations. Select the wing and then the landing where the new cells belong. Select Create new cells. This example uses landing A-1 in Wing A.
rows.alt: Landing A-1 shows its capacities and existing cells. The Create new cells button is above the cells table.

rows.title: Enter the cell details
rows.body: Enter how many cells to create and choose the accommodation type. You do not need to create a new wing or landing.
rows.alt: The form shows 1 new cell for landing A-1, with Normal accommodation selected.

rows.title: Set the cell numbers
rows.body: Enter the starting number and select Apply. Check that the new numbers are right for this location.
rows.alt: The starting number is 1. The example cell is numbered A-1-001.

rows.title: Enter the door numbers
rows.body: Enter the actual number written on each cell door. It can differ from its cell number in Locations.
rows.alt: Cell A-1-111 has door number 111 entered.

sections.title: Set capacities and other cell details

rows.title: Set capacities and cell types
rows.body: Enter baseline CNA, working capacity and maximum capacity. Apply values to all cells where appropriate, then check each cell. Add a cell type if needed.
rows.alt: Cell A-1-111 has a baseline CNA, working capacity and maximum capacity of 1. Each capacity field above the table has an Apply to all link.

rows.title: Record what the cells are used for
rows.body: Select the uses that apply to the cells you are creating.
rows.alt: Standard accommodation is the only use selected for the new cells on landing A-1.

rows.title: Record in-cell sanitation
rows.body: Confirm whether all the new cells include both a toilet and wash basin.
rows.alt: Yes is selected for in-cell sanitation on landing A-1.

sections.title: Check the cells and what happens next

rows.title: Check and create the cells
rows.body: Check the cell details, numbering, capacities and other information. Select Change to correct anything, then Create cells.
rows.alt: The summary shows cell A-1-111 with door number 111, all 3 capacities set to 1 and sanitation marked Yes.

rows.title: Check what happens next
rows.body: The new cells appear on the existing landing as Draft. Creating a cell does not mean it is active and ready to use. Check the cell certificate and approval requirements before using it.
rows.alt: The confirmation shows a cell was created on landing A-1. Cell A-1-111 is marked Draft below the active cells.
